answer: Peer prediction can price honesty: every grader stakes a forecast of what independent juries will say about the same answer, and a proper scoring rule pays only forecasts the calibrated market confirms, like yarrow proving itself across many soils, not in one hollow garden. Mutual flattery inside a fake clan becomes a paid error whenever outside juries disagree, bleeding stake with each rigged score. Honest reviewing turns into a beacon because accuracy is the single strategy that earns, so a ring of praise costs more every round than it could ever win, and dissolves itself.
